_comment: Hand-verified terrain ground truth. This is the calibration set: both the
detector and the semantic review pass are measured against it before being
trusted on the remaining tile faces.
Entries here are authored by someone reading the physical tiles, not
derived from the art by tooling, which is the whole point -- on Core_19B
the detector's accept/reject heuristic and an unaided review both
produced confident, specific and WRONG answers (close to the exact
complement of the truth). The flood-fill component, however, matched the
Glyphs: . normal  d difficult  X blocking  I impassable  P pit  - void

notes: The difficult terrain is the flooded/swamp area. Its boundary is formed
by the BLACK WALLS together with the blue lines, not by the blue lines
alone -- reading the blue in isolation is what inverted the answer.
The detector's blue flood-fill component matched this exactly (23/23).
Regions B (n=6), C (n=5) and D (n=2) are the raised grating platforms
NEGATIVE CONTROL. This tile is 14.9% red -- more red than any tile that
actually carries markings -- because it depicts a glowing vent. It has
no terrain markings at all. Any detector that classifies by hue without
requiring grid alignment fails here, and fails silently.
